memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Isaac stayed in Gerar. When the men of that place asked him about his wife, he said, 'She is my sister,' because he was afraid to say, 'She is my wife.' He thought, 'The men of this place might kill me on account of Rebekah, because she is beautiful.'" - Gen 26:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Isaac obeys God and stays in Gerar — but then fear takes over. Afraid the local men might kill him to take his beautiful wife, he lies: "She is my sister." It is a sad and familiar scene. His father Abraham had told the very same lie about Sarah, not once but twice (Gen 12; 20). Now the son repeats the father's failure.

This is a sobering reminder that the patterns we grow up around can shape us — sometimes for good, sometimes for ill. Isaac had likely heard the family story, yet in the pressure of the moment he fell into the same trap of fear-driven deception. Sinful patterns can be passed down almost without our noticing.

But there is hope here too. We are not helpless prisoners of our family's failures. When we recognise a pattern — a habit of lying, of fear, of anger, of running from problems — we can bring it honestly to God and ask Him to break the cycle. His grace is stronger than any inherited weakness.

Where do you see an old family pattern showing up in your own life? Name it before God. The Lord who is faithful can help you become the one in whom a harmful pattern finally ends, replaced by faith instead of fear.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What patterns from my upbringing show up in my own choices?
2. Where does fear tempt me to compromise the truth?
3. Am I bringing my inherited weaknesses honestly to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, where old patterns of fear and failure live in me, break the cycle by Your grace. Give me courage to walk in truth rather than fear. Amen.
